tool.name: well_known_harvest
tool.description:
Probe the standard `.well-known/` paths on a target host and emit one info-severity finding per hit (CWE-200, info_disclosure).
Modern domains have 5–15 well-known endpoints that leak architecture cleanly: - `security.txt` (RFC 9116) — security contact + disclosure policy + scope - `openid-configuration` — OpenID Connect tenant ID, OAuth endpoints, JWKS URL - `oauth-authorization-server` — OAuth 2.0 metadata - `change-password` (RFC 8615) — password-mgr-friendly redirect - `host-meta` (XRD / JSON) — WebFinger - `assetlinks.json` — Android digital asset link verification - `apple-app-site-association` — iOS universal-link / app-binding - `gpc.json` — Global Privacy Control declaration - Plus legacy: `/security.txt` (pre-RFC), `/humans.txt`, `/.well-known/dnt-policy.txt`
Hits are NOT vulns on their own — they're publicly-designed endpoints — but they reveal architecture which accelerates downstream reconnaissance and exploit chaining. The agent should read the parsed metadata and use it to plan deeper testing (e.g. OAuth endpoints from openid-configuration become targets for authz_matrix_check; security.txt's `contact` becomes the disclosure channel).
Composes with cluster-A safety (auth-injection / exclude-path / rate-limit) automatically — every fetch routes through the proxy or the direct fallback.
For domain-target scans, use this after `bfs_crawl` confirms the host is up; `bfs_crawl` itself doesn't probe these paths (it only crawls links it sees).

parameter.name: target
parameter.description: Target URL or hostname (e.g. `https://example.com` or `example.com`). The tool builds `/.well-known/` URLs from this — only the origin (scheme + host) matters; any path on the input is dropped.

parameter.name: include_legacy
parameter.description: When true (default), also probes legacy non-RFC-8615 locations: `/security.txt` (pre-RFC root), `/humans.txt`, `/.well-known/dnt-policy.txt`. Disable for strict RFC 8615 compliance.

returns.description:
{success, target, probed, hits: [{path, label, status, content_type, parsed, body_excerpt}], errors, stats}.
`parsed` is a small dict of structured fields (typically the OAuth endpoints from openid-configuration, the contact + policy fields from security.txt, the asset link relations from assetlinks.json, etc.). Findings are emitted as side effects via the tracer.
